source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus is the largest disclosed power block in Illinois at 114 MW of IT capacity, but most Illinois data centers disclose no megawatt figure at all.

The campus publishes 114 MW across three facility codes, CHI1 through CHI3, with 450,000 square feet of technical space. That is a power envelope, not a machine count. Converting it to racks requires an assumed density that the operator does not supply: at 40 kW per rack the figure implies roughly 2,850 racks, at 10 kW per rack about 11,400. The accelerator count depends on chips per rack, which is also unpublished. The rack and chip numbers are inferences, not facts from the spec page.

Within Illinois, this campus ranks first by published megawatts among the six facilities in the state that publish any figure. Those six total 236 MW, so Aurora alone is close to half of what the state has disclosed. The other 40 mapped facilities in Illinois publish nothing, which means the state's real capacity exceeds 236 MW and the ranking reflects disclosure rather than the full buildout.

For AI specifically, the constraint that matters is delivered and energized power, and the spec page does not say whether the 114 MW is built out or contracted. The only certification listed is Green Globes, which speaks to environmental design and not to any tenant or workload. Nothing published states who occupies the space or what hardware runs there. The physical siting within Aurora is also unestablished, since no address or postal code appears on the spec page.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
